answer: Cross-epoch drift scoring. Each identity's action vector is compared across epochs; large behavioural swings raise its drift score, and high drift caps its influence in the next epoch. Honest agents crossing a calm ocean of routine work keep low scores. An attacker running clones must hold each one steady for many epochs before it earns full weight, paying the summit of sustained consistency across every fake identity at once. Any abrupt pivot resets that clone's voyage toward influence, so scaling the fleet multiplies the wait.
